The invention described relates to a system and process for monitoring and evaluating clinical outcomes. This clinical outcome tracking and analysis covers patient sorting, outcome monitoring, quality-of-life measures, therapy-related toxicity, and the cost of care.

The system and method receive one or more input parameters. Examples of sorting parameters include sex, age, ethnicity, comorbid conditions, tobacco use, insurance source, medical record number, primary care physician, referring physician, hospital, approved service vendors, disease-specific clinical molecular phenotype, treatment intent, therapy stage, biomarkers, and care costs.

Using a clinical outcome tracking and analysis module run by a processor, multiple patient medical records are organized to identify a group of records that meet the selected parameter or parameters. A nodal address representing one or more variables is then applied to that organized group to identify a clinically relevant subset of patient medical records, namely those records within the sorted group that also satisfy the variable or variables.

The clinically relevant subset is then evaluated. Based on that evaluation, a communication is sent to a user in order to influence treatment, monitor performance, or reduce treatment variation, waste, or inefficiency while still achieving the intended clinical outcome.
outputs.L3:
The invention provides a system and method for tracking and analyzing clinical outcomes associated with patient care. The clinical outcomes may include, for example, quality of life, toxicity associated with a therapy, and cost of care. By collecting, organizing, and evaluating patient-related information, the system enables users to assess how different treatments, clinical practices, and patient characteristics affect outcomes over time.

In operation, the system receives one or more sorting parameters selected by a user or generated automatically. These sorting parameters may include patient demographics, comorbid conditions, insurance source, treating physicians, biomarkers, therapy stage, and cost-of-care information. The parameters may be used individually or in combination to define a population of interest for clinical review and analysis.

A clinical outcome tracking and analysis module then accesses a database of patient medical records and sorts the records based on the selected parameters. The module identifies patient records that match the selected criteria, thereby producing a subset of records relevant to the requested analysis. For example, the module may identify patients having a particular biomarker, receiving a specific therapy, being treated by a particular physician, or having costs within a defined range.

After the records are sorted, the system applies a nodal address to the sorted records. The nodal address contains one or more variables that further define or refine the patient population. These variables may represent clinical, demographic, financial, or treatment-related characteristics. Applying the nodal address allows the system to determine a clinically relevant set of patient records from the sorted records, thereby focusing the analysis on patients whose characteristics and treatment circumstances are meaningful for a particular clinical or operational question.

The system then analyzes the clinically relevant set of patient records to generate information regarding outcomes, treatment effectiveness, therapy toxicity, quality of life, resource utilization, cost of care, and other performance indicators. Based on this analysis, the system may generate and transmit communications to physicians, care teams, administrators, payors, or other authorized users. These communications may include reports, alerts, recommendations, comparisons, or other decision-support information.

In this manner, the system supports treatment decisions, monitors clinical and operational performance, and helps identify patterns of variability, waste, or inefficiency in care delivery. The system may also assist in improving consistency of treatment, evaluating the value of therapies, identifying patient groups at risk for poor outcomes, and enabling more informed decisions regarding patient management and resource allocation.
outputs.L4:
A clinical outcome tracking and analysis system is provided for collecting, organizing, filtering, and analyzing patient medical information in order to evaluate clinical outcomes and support improved healthcare decision-making. The system includes one or more processors configured to access patient medical records from electronic medical record systems, laboratory systems, pharmacy systems, billing systems, insurance databases, patient-reported outcome tools, provider databases, and other clinical or administrative data sources. The patient records may include demographic information, clinical history, diagnostic data, molecular or genomic test results, staging information, comorbidities, treatment regimens, therapy timing and sequencing, drug dosing, surgical and radiation treatment details, adverse events, toxicity measurements, quality-of-life indicators, insurance coverage information, provider characteristics, facility information, and cost data.

The system uses processor-executed sorting, classification, and nodal-variable filtering to identify and group patients into clinically meaningful cohorts. Nodal variables may include, for example, age, sex, race or ethnicity, diagnosis, disease subtype, disease stage, biomarker status, genetic mutation, prior therapy, line of therapy, treatment intent, performance status, toxicity profile, response to treatment, survival status, payer type, treating provider, treatment location, and total cost of care. By applying one or more of these variables individually or in combination, the system can generate patient cohorts that share defined clinical, molecular, demographic, therapeutic, financial, or operational characteristics.

Once cohorts are identified, the system analyzes outcomes associated with each cohort. Outcome measures may include overall survival, progression-free survival, disease-free survival, response rate, hospitalization rate, emergency department use, treatment discontinuation, dose modification, adverse event frequency, toxicity severity, patient-reported quality of life, adherence to clinical pathways or guidelines, resource utilization, and cost of care. The system may compare outcomes across different treatments, providers, institutions, payer groups, or patient subpopulations. It may also identify variations in care patterns, differences in clinical effectiveness, differences in toxicity burden, and differences in economic impact.

The system may generate dashboards, reports, alerts, visualizations, and decision-support outputs for clinicians, administrators, payers, researchers, and other authorized users. These outputs may assist users in selecting treatment options, monitoring patient progress, evaluating provider or institutional performance, identifying best practices, measuring compliance with evidence-based pathways, and assessing the value of particular therapies or interventions. The system may also support retrospective analyses, prospective cohort tracking, quality improvement initiatives, clinical research, value-based care programs, and population health management.

By integrating diverse clinical, molecular, patient-reported, operational, insurance, provider, and cost parameters, the system enables a more comprehensive assessment of real-world treatment outcomes. The system helps identify clinically relevant patient cohorts, evaluate the effectiveness and safety of therapies in those cohorts, and detect sources of unwarranted variation in care. As a result, the system can support improved treatment decisions, enhanced performance monitoring, more consistent delivery of evidence-based care, reduced toxicity and patient burden, decreased inefficiency and waste, and lower overall healthcare costs.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, a system and method for analyzing clinical outcomes using patient record sorting, nodal variables, quality-of-life metrics, toxicity tracking, and communications to improve treatment decisions.
counterfactuals.output:
A computerized system and method are disclosed for analyzing clinical outcomes and supporting treatment decision-making. The system comprises one or more processors, memory storing executable instructions, a patient-record data repository, a sorting and stratification engine, a nodal-variable analysis module, a quality-of-life assessment module, a toxicity tracking module, and a communications interface configured to exchange clinical information among authorized users.

In one embodiment, the system receives patient records comprising demographic data, diagnostic data, staging information, pathology data, laboratory values, imaging findings, genomic or biomarker information, prior treatment history, treatment regimens, outcome data, adverse-event data, and patient-reported quality-of-life information. The patient records are normalized into a common data structure and are sorted according to one or more clinical parameters, including disease type, disease stage, treatment modality, response category, recurrence status, survival interval, toxicity grade, quality-of-life score, and selected nodal variables.

The nodal variables may include lymph-node status, number of involved nodes, nodal station, nodal burden, nodal ratio, extracapsular extension, sentinel-node status, regional spread patterns, or other anatomically or clinically relevant nodal descriptors. The system associates the nodal variables with treatment parameters and clinical outcomes to identify correlations, risk patterns, or predictive groupings relevant to selection, modification, or evaluation of therapy.

The quality-of-life assessment module receives, stores, and analyzes patient-reported outcome measures, including physical function, pain, fatigue, emotional well-being, social function, symptom burden, treatment satisfaction, and activity limitations. The module may calculate longitudinal quality-of-life trajectories and compare said trajectories across patient cohorts, treatment regimens, toxicity profiles, or nodal-variable classifications.

The toxicity tracking module records treatment-related adverse events, including onset date, severity, duration, intervention, dose modification, hospitalization, resolution status, and grading according to a standardized toxicity scale. The toxicity data are linked to corresponding treatment exposures, quality-of-life metrics, and outcome measures to determine tolerability patterns and to identify patient subgroups at elevated risk for adverse effects.

The sorting and stratification engine generates patient cohorts by applying one or more user-selected or automatically selected criteria to the patient records. The cohorts may be analyzed to determine outcome measures including overall survival, progression-free survival, disease-free survival, recurrence rate, response rate, complication rate, toxicity incidence, treatment discontinuation rate, quality-of-life change, and composite clinical-benefit scores. The system may further generate comparative analyses between cohorts receiving different treatments or having different nodal-variable profiles.

In certain embodiments, the system applies statistical, rule-based, or machine-learning techniques to identify relationships among nodal variables, treatment regimens, quality-of-life metrics, toxicity events, and clinical outcomes. The system may generate a risk score, benefit score, toxicity probability, quality-of-life prediction, treatment-response prediction, or ranked treatment option for a patient or patient cohort. The generated output may include confidence values, explanatory factors, comparative cohort data, and recommendations for additional review.

The communications interface transmits alerts, reports, dashboards, treatment summaries, outcome comparisons, toxicity notifications, and quality-of-life updates to authorized clinicians, care teams, researchers, or patient-facing portals. The communications may be configured to notify a clinician when a toxicity threshold is exceeded, when a quality-of-life metric declines beyond a predetermined amount, when a patient matches a high-risk nodal-variable profile, or when an alternative treatment pathway is associated with improved outcomes in a comparable cohort.

A method implemented by the system includes: receiving a plurality of patient records; normalizing the patient records into a standardized clinical data format; sorting the patient records based on selected clinical parameters; identifying and encoding nodal variables within the patient records; receiving quality-of-life metrics from clinical assessments or patient-reported instruments; receiving toxicity data associated with one or more treatments; correlating the nodal variables, quality-of-life metrics, toxicity data, treatment data, and clinical outcome data; generating one or more patient-specific or cohort-specific outcome analyses; and communicating the analyses to authorized users to support treatment planning, monitoring, modification, or selection.

In some embodiments, the method further comprises continuously updating the patient-record repository as new clinical events occur, recalculating risk or outcome models based on the updated records, and producing revised treatment-support outputs. The system may maintain audit logs, access controls, de-identification functions, encryption, and compliance controls to protect patient information while enabling clinical outcome analysis.

The disclosed system and method thereby provide an integrated clinical decision-support platform that combines patient record sorting, nodal-variable evaluation, patient-centered quality-of-life assessment, toxicity surveillance, and structured communications to improve the selection, adjustment, and evaluation of treatments.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft the “summary of the invention” section for a medical informatics patent covering outcome tracking, therapy toxicity, cost-of-care analysis, and reduction of treatment variability and inefficiency.
counterfactuals.output:
## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to medical informatics systems and methods for monitoring, analyzing, and improving patient care. More particularly, the invention provides computer-implemented systems and methods for integrating clinical, operational, financial, and patient-reported information to track treatment outcomes, evaluate therapy-related toxicity, analyze cost of care, and reduce variability and inefficiency in the delivery of medical treatment.

In one aspect, the invention provides a medical informatics platform configured to receive patient-specific data from one or more data sources, including electronic health records, laboratory systems, pharmacy systems, claims systems, scheduling systems, imaging systems, registries, and patient-reported outcome tools. The platform may normalize, map, and aggregate the received data into a longitudinal patient record associated with one or more diagnoses, treatment regimens, care pathways, treatment episodes, or disease states.

In another aspect, the invention provides methods for tracking clinical outcomes associated with one or more therapies. The system may identify a patient cohort based on diagnosis, disease stage, biomarker status, comorbidities, demographic characteristics, treatment regimen, treating provider, practice site, payer, or other clinical or non-clinical attributes. For each cohort, the system may determine outcome measures including, without limitation, response rate, disease progression, survival, hospitalization, emergency department utilization, treatment discontinuation, dose modification, quality-of-life measures, functional status, symptom burden, adherence, and other clinical endpoints. The system may generate comparative outcome analytics across therapies, providers, sites of care, patient subgroups, or time periods.

In another aspect, the invention provides systems and methods for monitoring therapy toxicity. The platform may detect, classify, and grade treatment-related adverse events using structured data, unstructured clinical notes, laboratory values, medication orders, diagnosis codes, procedure codes, patient-reported symptoms, or combinations thereof. The system may correlate toxicities with specific drugs, combinations of drugs, dosing schedules, patient characteristics, laboratory trends, genomic markers, prior therapies, or comorbidities. The platform may further generate toxicity profiles for therapies and cohorts, identify patients at elevated risk of toxicity, and provide alerts, recommendations, or workflow prompts to clinicians or care teams.

In another aspect, the invention provides systems and methods for cost-of-care analysis. The platform may associate clinical events and treatment episodes with cost data, including drug acquisition costs, administration costs, facility fees, professional fees, laboratory costs, imaging costs, hospitalization costs, emergency department costs, supportive care costs, adverse-event management costs, payer reimbursement amounts, patient out-of-pocket costs, and other resource utilization measures. The system may compute cost metrics per patient, per treatment episode, per regimen, per pathway, per provider, per site, per payer, or per outcome achieved. In certain embodiments, the platform may calculate total cost of care, cost per response, cost per toxicity avoided, cost per progression-free interval, cost per quality-adjusted measure, or other value-based care metrics.

In another aspect, the invention provides methods for reducing treatment variability. The system may compare actual treatment decisions, drug selections, dosing, sequencing, monitoring, supportive care measures, and follow-up practices against evidence-based guidelines, institutional pathways, payer policies, regulatory indications, clinical trial protocols, or locally defined best practices. The platform may identify deviations from a pathway or standard of care and may determine whether the deviations are clinically justified based on patient-specific factors. The system may generate reports, dashboards, alerts, or recommendations that enable providers, administrators, payers, or quality improvement personnel to identify and reduce unwarranted variation in care.

In another aspect, the invention provides methods for reducing inefficiency in medical treatment delivery. The platform may identify redundant testing, avoidable emergency department visits, preventable admissions, treatment delays, missed appointments, unnecessary therapy changes, excessive toxicity-related interventions, underuse or overuse of supportive care, inappropriate site-of-care selection, and other inefficiencies. The system may generate actionable recommendations to optimize scheduling, drug utilization, monitoring frequency, supportive care, patient outreach, care coordination, and resource allocation.

In certain embodiments, the invention includes a rules engine, analytics engine, machine learning model, or combination thereof configured to generate patient-specific or cohort-level insights. The system may use historical clinical and cost data to predict outcomes, toxicity risk, likelihood of hospitalization, expected cost of care, probability of pathway deviation, or expected benefit of an intervention. In some embodiments, predictive models may be updated using new patient data and outcomes, thereby enabling continuous learning and refinement of treatment recommendations, risk stratification, and cost predictions.

In certain embodiments, the platform generates one or more graphical user interfaces, dashboards, reports, or alerts. Such interfaces may display longitudinal treatment timelines, outcome measures, toxicity events, care pathway adherence, cost drivers, utilization metrics, cohort comparisons, provider-level variation, site-level variation, payer-specific metrics, and patient-specific risk indicators. The interfaces may support drill-down analysis from population-level metrics to individual patient records and may enable filtering by clinical, demographic, operational, and financial variables.

In certain embodiments, the invention supports value-based care arrangements by linking clinical outcomes, toxicity burden, and cost of care to episodes of treatment or defined patient cohorts. The system may generate performance measures suitable for quality reporting, contract management, payer negotiation, bundled payment evaluation, shared savings analysis, or risk adjustment. The system may further identify opportunities to improve value by selecting therapies, care pathways, monitoring strategies, or supportive interventions associated with improved outcomes, reduced toxicity, lower cost, or reduced variability.

In another aspect, the invention provides a computer-implemented method comprising: receiving patient data from one or more clinical and financial data sources; normalizing the patient data into a common data model; associating the normalized data with a treatment episode; determining one or more outcome measures for the treatment episode; detecting one or more toxicity events associated with the treatment episode; determining one or more cost-of-care measures associated with the treatment episode; comparing the treatment episode to one or more care pathways or benchmark cohorts; identifying variation or inefficiency in the treatment episode; and generating at least one output comprising an alert, recommendation, score, dashboard, report, or workflow action for improving care delivery.

In another aspect, the invention provides a system comprising one or more processors and one or more non-transitory computer-readable media storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the system to perform operations for outcome tracking, toxicity monitoring, cost-of-care analysis, pathway adherence analysis, and treatment variability reduction. The system may be deployed as a cloud-based platform, local server, distributed computing environment, software-as-a-service platform, integrated electronic health record module, or hybrid architecture.

In another aspect, the invention provides a non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the processors to perform any of the methods described herein.

The invention thereby enables integrated assessment of the clinical effectiveness, safety, economic impact, and operational consistency of medical therapies. By correlating outcomes, toxicities, resource utilization, and adherence to preferred practices, the invention supports improved clinical decision-making, more efficient care delivery, reduced unwarranted treatment variation, and enhanced value in healthcare.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an AI-generated patent claim-style description for a clinical outcome tracking module executed by a processor that filters patient records by variables such as age, sex, ethnicity, comorbidities, biomarkers, physicians, hospitals, and insurance source.
counterfactuals.output:
1. A computer-implemented clinical outcome tracking module, comprising:  
   one or more processors; and  
   a non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform operations comprising:

   receiving a plurality of patient records from one or more clinical data sources, each patient record including at least one clinical outcome indicator and one or more patient-associated variables;

   normalizing the plurality of patient records into a structured data format suitable for comparative analysis;

   filtering the plurality of patient records according to one or more selected variables comprising age, sex, ethnicity, comorbidities, biomarkers, treating physician, hospital, and insurance source;

   generating, based on the filtered plurality of patient records, an outcome data set corresponding to a defined patient cohort;

   determining one or more clinical outcome metrics for the defined patient cohort, the one or more clinical outcome metrics comprising at least one of treatment response, adverse event rate, hospitalization rate, readmission rate, disease progression, survival, mortality, medication adherence, or cost of care;

   comparing the one or more clinical outcome metrics across at least two filtered cohorts differentiated by one or more of the selected variables; and

   outputting, to a user interface, a report indicating variations in clinical outcomes associated with the selected variables.

2. The module of claim 1, wherein the operations further comprise generating a graphical dashboard displaying cohort-specific outcome trends over time.

3. The module of claim 1, wherein the patient-associated variables include biomarker values selected from genomic markers, laboratory values, imaging-derived markers, pathology markers, or physiologic measurements.

4. The module of claim 1, wherein the comorbidities are identified from diagnostic codes, medication records, procedure records, physician notes, or a combination thereof.

5. The module of claim 1, wherein the filtering comprises applying multiple simultaneous filter criteria to identify a subgroup of patients sharing a selected combination of demographic, clinical, provider, institutional, and payer characteristics.

6. The module of claim 1, wherein the operations further comprise risk-adjusting the one or more clinical outcome metrics based on baseline patient characteristics.

7. The module of claim 1, wherein the report includes comparative outcome information stratified by physician, hospital, or insurance source.

8. The module of claim 1, wherein the clinical data sources comprise one or more of an electronic health record system, claims database, laboratory information system, pharmacy database, disease registry, or patient-reported outcome platform.

9. The module of claim 1, wherein the operations further comprise detecting statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes among filtered cohorts.

10. The module of claim 1, wherein the output report includes a recommendation, alert, or flag identifying a patient subgroup associated with an elevated risk of an adverse clinical outcome.
